title: Severe Obstetric & Postpartum Hemorrhage Emergency
sourceOrganization: Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH) & WHO
summary: Sudden heavy bleeding soaking more than one cloth/pad per hour, large clots, or bleeding accompanied by dizziness constitutes an acute surgical emergency.
keyPoints: Soaking >1 pad or clean cloth within 1 hour indicates severe life-threatening hemorrhage.
Warning signs of hemorrhagic shock: rapid thready pulse, cold clammy hands, dizziness, fainting, and confusion.
Requires immediate emergency hospital transport for uterotonic medicines (Oxytocin, Misoprostol), IV fluids, and blood transfusion.
Keep the mother warm and lying flat with legs slightly elevated during ambulance transport.
detailedContent: Obstetric hemorrhage is the leading cause of preventable maternal mortality worldwide.

In Ethiopia, public hospital emergency maternity units are mandated to provide immediate triage, active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL), and blood banking services without financial prepayment.
whenToSeeClinician: Call 907 (Red Cross Ambulance) or 952 (EMS) immediately, or take the patient directly to the nearest Hospital Emergency Ward.
ethiopiaContext: Free emergency obstetric surgery and blood transfusion at all Ethiopian public secondary and tertiary hospitals.

title: Pre-eclampsia & Eclampsia (Severe High Blood Pressure & Fits)
summary: Severe headache that does not respond to painkillers, blurred or flashing vision, epigastric pain, or seizures in pregnancy or postpartum.
keyPoints: Pre-eclampsia involves dangerous elevation of blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg) with proteinuria after 20 weeks of pregnancy.
Key red flags: pounding headache, seeing spots/blurriness, swelling of face and hands, pain under right ribs.
Eclampsia occurs when high blood pressure triggers convulsions/seizures, threatening maternal oxygenation and fetal life.
Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) is the proven standard-of-care injectable anticonvulsant administered in hospital delivery wards.
detailedContent: Health centers in Ethiopia carry emergency loading doses of Magnesium Sulfate and antihypertensives before initiating transfer to higher-level referral hospitals.
Never leave a convulsing woman unattended; place her on her left side to protect the airway and facilitate placental blood flow.
whenToSeeClinician: Proceed immediately to the nearest hospital emergency room. Do not delay or wait for headache medication to take effect.
ethiopiaContext: Primary loading dose of Magnesium Sulfate available across public Health Centers and General Hospitals in Ethiopia.

title: Confidential Care for Sexual Assault & Hospital One-Stop Centers
sourceOrganization: UNFPA Ethiopia & Ethiopian Ministry of Health
summary: Comprehensive, compassionate survivor care providing free HIV PEP within 72 hours, emergency contraception, trauma therapy, and legal support in a private room.
keyPoints: Visit a hospital One-Stop Center strictly within 72 hours to receive HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP).
Receive emergency contraception within 72 to 120 hours to prevent unintended pregnancy.
One-Stop Centers provide medical care, psychological first aid, forensic documentation, and legal support in a single confidential space.
Toll-free 24/7 helplines in Ethiopia: AWSAD Safe Shelter 6226, FMoH Helpline 8335, Marie Stopes 8044.
detailedContent: Survivors of sexual assault face time-sensitive physical and emotional vulnerabilities.

Hospital One-Stop Centers operate at public hospitals across Addis Ababa (e.g. Gandhi Memorial, Yekatit 12, Tirunesh Beijing) and regional referral centers (Hawassa, Jimma, Bahir Dar, Mekelle, Adama).
All medical services are free, confidential, and provided without police presence if the survivor chooses medical care only.
ethiopiaContext: One-Stop Centers established at major public referral hospitals in all regional states; helpline AWSAD 6226.

title: Emergency Drone Blood & Life-Saving Supply Logistics Pilot
sourceOrganization: Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI) & Zipline Pilot
summary: Draft summary of aerial drone delivery trials for emergency blood products and anti-hemorrhage medications to remote health centers.
keyPoints: Automated drone distribution system transporting emergency whole blood, platelets, and postpartum oxytocics within 30 minutes.
Targeting hard-to-reach rural health centers in highland and pastoralist woredas cut off by seasonal floods or rugged topography.
Clinicians place instant SMS or satellite dispatch requests to regional distribution hubs.
Currently active in designated demonstration corridors pending national civil aviation expansion.
detailedContent: Draft clinical notes: Protocols for cold-chain maintenance and remote landing zone receiver training for health center nurses.
Under review by the EPHI Emergency Logistics Directorate.
whenToSeeClinician: Health workers in participating pilot woredas can request urgent blood via the EPHI Emergency Logistics hotline.
ethiopiaContext: Piloted in selected rural regional districts under Ethiopian Public Health Institute supervision.
